title: Anchor Objectives: lightweight commitment contract to bind roadmaps to company OKRs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: company-level OKRs are clear, but teams struggle to translate them into bounded, commitable roadmap slices. Current practices oscillate between no governance (leads to misalignment) and heavyweight contracts (slows teams and blocks velocity).

Goal: create an "Anchor Objectives" template and lightweight protocol that lets PMs and Eng leads declare a bounded, measurable commitment (the anchor) that maps to a company OKR, plus clear escalation and decommit rules. The anchor should be usable in our roadmap tools and visible in the Console’s initiative view.

What success looks like:
- 5 pilot teams adopt Anchor Objectives for their next planning cycle (Cycle 53)
- 80% of anchors have clear metrics + a definition of done, visible in the initiative dashboard
- Reduction in post-quarter scope churn for anchored initiatives by 30% (pilot teams)

Scope and deliverables:
1) Anchor template (fields + examples): objective mapping, owner, committed scope (not >2 deliverables), leading indicators, fallback/degrade plan, ripple allowance (max % of tasks that can be decommitted without escalation).
2) Lightweight protocol doc: timelines for anchor creation (T-4 weeks before cycle), acceptance gates, sign-offs (PM, Eng Lead, Design where applicable), and the decommit/escalation flow.
3) Instrumentation checklist: tags in Linear, dashboard widgets in Console (OKR-to-initiative link), and a minimal rollout report for GTM & exec syncs.
4) Pilot run with 5 teams + retrospective and iteration.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict enforcement vs. trust model: we opt for a trust-oriented, opt-in pilot to avoid process burden. If adoption is low, we’ll iterate to add automated gating.
- Granularity: anchors must be big enough to be meaningful but small enough to remain commitable. We default to "1-2 deliverables" per anchor to strike this balance.

Open questions:
- How to quantify "ripple allowance" across different work types (infra vs. product)? Proposed: percent-of-scope baseline with separate rules for infra tasks.
- How to show anchors in Console with minimal eng effort? Can we reuse existing initiative tagging and a single additional boolean flag?

Next steps (owner):
- Draft anchor template + 3 example anchors (Aisha) — due 2026-02-12 (DONE)
- Review template with Eng Leads + Design (Marco) — in progress, scheduled 2026-02-18 (feedback captured below)
- Implement Linear tags + acceptance gate (ENG: ENG-1842) — blocked on priority queue, ETA 2026-03-01
- Build pilot dashboard (Product Analytics) — requested, awaiting dataset (PA owner: Jenna Park)

Why this is different: rather than another OKR framework, Anchor Objectives are a binding but lightweight commitment pattern that preserves team autonomy while creating reliable signal for cross-team planning and exec reporting.
